title: Introduction and fundamentals
subtitle: Build the language and habits that support every later SAT Math topic.

isi: This first meeting establishes the habits and language needed for the entire SAT Math course. You will learn how the Digital SAT Math section is organized, what kinds of mathematical content can appear, how to use the built-in Desmos calculator and reference information, and how to translate everyday language into mathematical expressions.

The central idea is mathematical modeling: a word problem describes a situation, and you build a mathematical representation of that situation. A strong model uses variables carefully, preserves units, and translates phrases such as at least, twice, per, and no more than accurately.

items: Identify the quantity or relationship the question asks for.
Build a mathematical model from the wording.
Verify that the result fits the situation.

isi.content: The Math section has two modules. Each module contains 22 questions and has a 35-minute time limit. The second module is adaptive: performance in the first module influences the difficulty level of the second module.
Questions may be multiple-choice, with four answer choices, or student-produced response, in which you enter a numerical answer directly.
For a student-produced response, enter a number, decimal point, fraction slash, or negative sign as appropriate. A mixed number such as \(4\frac{1}{2}\) may be entered as \(\frac{9}{2}\) or \(4.5\).

items.title: Arithmetic
items.content: Fractions, ratios, percentages, exponents, radicals, and complex numbers.

items.title: Algebra
items.content: Equations, inequalities, functions, systems, quadratics, exponentials, logarithms, and circles.

items.title: Geometry
items.content: Lines, angles, triangles, area, volume, surface area, and transformations.

items.title: Statistics
items.content: Tables, graphs, averages, probability, sampling, and data claims.

isi: The purpose of this meeting is not to master every topic immediately. It is to build a map of the test and make sure the algebraic language underneath later topics is secure.
A variable represents an unknown or changing quantity. In the expression \(3x+5\), the number 3 is the coefficient of \(x\), and 5 is a constant.
When defining a variable, give it meaning. For example, write “Let \(x\) be the number of tickets,” rather than only writing “Let \(x\).”

rows: The value of \(x\) is two times \(y\).

isi.content: The order matters. “Three less than \(x\)” is \(x-3\), not \(3-x\).

isi: An equation states equality. An inequality describes a range of possible values.

rows: The value is greater than or equal to.
at most / maximum / no more than
The value is less than or equal to.

isi: Units help prevent modeling errors. If one notebook costs USD 4 and a student buys \(n\) notebooks, the cost is:
If a phone call costs USD 0.20 per minute and lasts \(h\) hours, first convert hours to minutes:

isi.content: Keep track of dollars, minutes, pounds, students, and other units. Convert before combining quantities measured in different units.

isi: Desmos is especially useful for graphing equations and inequalities, finding intersections, checking zeros and intercepts, evaluating numerical expressions, and exploring the meaning of parameters.
The reference sheet is useful for geometry formulas. However, a formula is only helpful when you know what each quantity represents.

isi.content: Use a tool after identifying the mathematical relationship. A graph or calculator can verify a model, but it should not replace the modeling step.

isi.title: Example 1: Translate a comparison
isi.content: Andy’s height is \(x\) centimeters. Bryan is 3 centimeters taller. “Taller than” means add, so Bryan’s height is \(x+3\).

isi.title: Example 2: Translate a repeated cost
isi.content: One book costs USD \(d\). The cost of \(n\) books is \(nd\) dollars.

isi.title: Example 3: Build a linear model
isi.content: A bicycle rental shop charges a fixed fee of USD 8 plus USD 3 per hour. After \(t\) hours, the cost is \(C=3t+8\). For 5 hours, \(C=3(5)+8=23\), so the total cost is USD 23.

isi.title: Example 4: Translate a capacity restriction
isi.content: A school accepts no more than 1,000 students. If \(b\) is the number of boys and \(g\) is the number of girls, then \(b+g\le1000\).

isi.title: Example 5: Use the definition of an intercept
isi.content: The y-intercept of \(y=-6x-32\) occurs when \(x=0\). Therefore \(y=-6(0)-32=-32\), and the y-intercept is \((0,-32)\).

items: Underline relational phrases such as “per,” “at least,” “twice,” and “no more than.”
Preserve units and convert when necessary.
Check the scale and whether the answer fits the context.
Use Desmos to verify an intersection or intercept when useful.

latihan.question: Why should I learn Math Modelling?
latihan.answer: Because many SAT questions involve translating words into mathematical equations and translating equations back into words, especially in word problems.
discussion: Mathematical modeling connects a real-world situation to a mathematical representation.
This skill helps identify variables, relationships, units, and the equation that represents the situation.

latihan.question: Andy's height is \(x\), and Bryan is 3 cm taller than Andy. What is Bryan's height?
discussion: “3 cm taller than Andy” means add 3 to Andy's height.
Bryan's height is \(x+3\).

latihan.question: The price of a pen is \(x\), and the price of a pencil is 2 cents less than that of the pen. What is the price of the pencil?
discussion: “2 cents less than” means subtract 2.
The pencil's price is \(x-2\) cents.

latihan.question: The price of one book is \(d\). What is the price of \(n\) books?
discussion: The total price is the price of one book multiplied by the number of books.
The model is \(nd\) dollars.

latihan.question: The price of one mango is \(x\), and the price of one guava is double the price of the mango. What is the price of the guava?
discussion: “Double the price of the mango” means multiply \(x\) by 2.
The guava's price is \(2x\).

latihan.question: There are only \(m\) apples and \(n\) oranges in a basket. How many fruits are there in total in the basket?
discussion: The total number of fruits is the number of apples plus the number of oranges.
The total is \(m+n\).

latihan.question: A teacher brings \(b\) books to the class to be divided equally among \(s\) students. How many books does every student get?
discussion: Dividing \(b\) books equally among \(s\) students means divide \(b\) by \(s\).
Every student gets \(\frac{b}{s}\) books.

latihan.question: Let \(x\) be the number of students. Classify which statement belongs to which notation:
latihan.prompt:
Notation:

  1. \(x=30\)
  2. \(x<30\)
  3. \(x\le30\)
  4. \(x>30\)
  5. \(x\ge30\)

Statements:

  1. The number of students is equal to 30.
  2. The number of students is more/greater than 30.
  3. The number of students is more than or equal to 30.
  4. The number of students is less than 30.
  5. The number of students is less than or equal to 30.
  6. The number of students is at least/cannot be less than 30.
  7. The number of students is at most/cannot be greater than 30.
  8. The number of students cannot exceed 30.
  9. The maximum number of students is 30.
  10. The minimum number of students is 30.
  11. The exact number of students is 30.
discussion: Statements a and k describe exactly 30, so they match \(x=30\).
Statement d describes fewer than 30, so it matches \(x<30\).
Statements e, g, h, and i describe at most 30, so they match \(x\le30\).
Statement b describes more than 30, so it matches \(x>30\).
Statements c, f, and j describe at least 30, so they match \(x\ge30\).

latihan.question: The price of a shirt is \(s\), and the price of a hat is \(h\). How much should Andy pay for \(n\) shirts and \(m\) hats?
discussion: The cost of \(n\) shirts is \(ns\) dollars.
The cost of \(m\) hats is \(mh\) dollars.
The total cost is \(ns+mh\) dollars.

latihan.question: A school can only accept no more than 1,000 students per year. The school accepts \(b\) boys and \(g\) girls. Create a mathematical model involving \(b\), \(g\), and 1,000 for this situation.
discussion: The total number of students is \(b+g\).
“No more than 1,000” means the total can be 1,000 or less.
The model is \(b+g\le1000\).

latihan.question: One pound of grapes costs $2. At this rate, how many dollars will \(c\) pounds of grapes cost?
discussion: The rate is 2 dollars per pound.
For \(c\) pounds, multiply the rate by the number of pounds: \(2c\).

latihan.question: When 4 times the number \(x\) is added to 12, the result is 8. What number results when 2 times \(x\) is added to 7?
discussion: Translate the first statement: \(4x+12=8\).
The correct choice is 5, which is option B.

latihan.question: On Saturday afternoon, Armand sent \(m\) text messages each hour for 5 hours, and Tyrone sent \(p\) text messages each hour for 4 hours. Which of the following represents the total number of messages sent by Armand and Tyrone on Saturday afternoon?
discussion: Armand sent \(5m\) messages.
Tyrone sent \(4p\) messages.
The total is \(5m+4p\).

latihan.question: The cost of using a telephone in a hotel meeting room is $0.20 per minute. Which of the following equations represents the total cost \(c\), in dollars, for \(h\) hours of phone use?
discussion: The rate is given per minute, so convert \(h\) hours to \(60h\) minutes.
Multiply the number of minutes by 0.20 dollars per minute: \(c=0.20(60h)\).

latihan.question: A gardener buys two kinds of fertilizer. Fertilizer A contains 60% filler materials by weight and Fertilizer B contains 40% filler materials by weight. Together, the fertilizers bought by the gardener contain a total of 240 pounds of filler materials. Which equation models this relationship, where \(x\) is the number of pounds of Fertilizer A and \(y\) is the number of pounds of Fertilizer B?
discussion: Fertilizer A contributes \(0.60x\) pounds of filler materials.
Fertilizer B contributes \(0.40y\) pounds of filler materials.
The total is 240 pounds, so \(0.6x+0.4y=240\).

latihan.question: Two types of tickets were sold for a concert held at an amphitheater. Tickets to sit on a bench during the concert cost $75 each, and tickets to sit on the lawn during the concert cost $40 each. Organizers of the concert announced that 350 tickets had been sold and that $19,250 had been raised through ticket sales alone. Which of the following systems of equations could be used to find the number of tickets for bench seats, \(B\), and the number of tickets for lawn seats, \(L\), that were sold for the concert?
discussion: The total number of tickets is \(B+L=350\).
The ticket revenue is \(75B+40L=19{,}250\).
Together, these equations form option D.

latihan.question: Roberto is an insurance agent who sells two types of policies: a $50,000 policy and a $100,000 policy. Last month, his goal was to sell at least 57 insurance policies. While he did not meet his goal, the total value of the policies he sold was over $3,000,000. Which of the following systems of inequalities describes \(x\), the possible number of $50,000 policies, and \(y\), the possible number of $100,000 policies, that Roberto sold last month?
discussion: He did not meet a goal of at least 57 policies, so \(x+y<57\).
This is option C.

latihan.question: A laundry service is buying detergent and fabric softener from its supplier. The supplier will deliver no more than 300 pounds in a shipment. Each container of detergent weighs 7.35 pounds, and each container of fabric softener weighs 6.2 pounds. The service wants to buy at least twice as many containers of detergent as containers of fabric softener. Let \(d\) represent the number of containers of detergent, and let \(s\) represent the number of containers of fabric softener, where \(d\) and \(s\) are nonnegative integers. Which of the following systems of inequalities best represents this situation?
discussion: The shipment weight is \(7.35d+6.2s\), and no more than 300 pounds means \(7.35d+6.2s\le300\).
At least twice as many detergent containers means \(d\ge2s\).
The correct system is option A.

additionalPractice.question: A notebook costs USD 4. If Maya buys \(n\) notebooks, which expression represents the total cost?
discussion: The cost of one notebook is USD 4.
For \(n\) notebooks, multiply 4 by \(n\): \(4n\).

additionalPractice.question: Leo is 5 years older than Ana, whose age is \(a\). Which expression represents Leo's age?
discussion: “5 years older than Ana” means add 5 to Ana's age.
Leo's age is \(a+5\).

additionalPractice.question: A school has \(b\) boys and \(g\) girls. Which expression represents the total number of students?
discussion: The total number of students is the number of boys plus the number of girls.
The expression is \(b+g\).

additionalPractice.question: A movie theater can hold no more than 450 people. If \(x\) people are inside, which inequality represents the situation?
discussion: “No more than 450” means the number can be 450 or less.
The inequality is \(x\le450\).

additionalPractice.question: A fruit basket contains \(r\) red apples and \(y\) yellow apples. Which expression represents the number of apples remaining after 3 apples are removed?
discussion: The basket initially contains \(r+y\) apples.
Removing 3 apples gives \(r+y-3\).

additionalPractice.question: A music service charges a fixed fee of USD 7 plus USD 2 for each downloaded album. Which equation represents the total cost \(C\) for \(a\) albums?
discussion: The fixed fee is the constant 7.
The cost for \(a\) albums is \(2a\).
Therefore, \(C=2a+7\).

additionalPractice.question: A number \(x\) is multiplied by 3 and then decreased by 8 to produce 19. What is \(x\)?
discussion: Translate the statement as \(3x-8=19\).
Add 8 to both sides: \(3x=27\).
Divide by 3: \(x=9\).

additionalPractice.question: A school admits \(m\) students in the morning and twice as many students in the afternoon. If the school admits 96 students in total, which equation can be used to find \(m\)?
discussion: The morning enrollment is \(m\).
The afternoon enrollment is twice as many, or \(2m\).
The total is \(m+2m=96\).

additionalPractice.question: The number of red cards in a collection is 4 fewer than twice the number of blue cards. If \(r\) is the number of red cards and \(b\) is the number of blue cards, which equation represents the relationship?
discussion: Twice the number of blue cards is \(2b\).
Four fewer than \(2b\) is \(2b-4\).
Therefore, \(r=2b-4\).

additionalPractice.question: A school accepts at least 300 applicants but no more than 500 applicants. If \(x\) is the number accepted, which system represents the situation?
discussion: “At least 300” means \(x\ge300\).
“No more than 500” means \(x\le500\).
Together, \(300\le x\le500\).

additionalPractice.question: A delivery company charges USD 18 for the first 10 miles and USD 1.40 for each additional mile. Which piecewise model represents the cost \(C\) for \(d\) miles, where \(d>0\)?
discussion: The first 10 miles cost a fixed USD 18.
Only miles beyond 10 receive the additional USD 1.40 charge.
For \(d>10\), the additional distance is \(d-10\), giving \(C=18+1.40(d-10)\).

additionalPractice.question: A school has \(x\) ninth-grade students and \(y\) tenth-grade students. The number of tenth-grade students is 24 more than the number of ninth-grade students, and the total number of students is 416. Which system represents the situation?
discussion: The tenth-grade count is 24 more than the ninth-grade count, so \(y=x+24\).
The total number of students is \(x+y=416\).

additionalPractice.question: A quantity is increased by 40% and then decreased by 25%. If the original quantity is \(q\), which expression represents the final quantity?
discussion: Increasing by 40% multiplies the quantity by \(1.40\).
Decreasing the new quantity by 25% multiplies it by \(0.75\).
The final quantity is \(q(1.40)(0.75)\).

additionalPractice.question: A theater sells adult tickets for USD 14 and student tickets for USD 9. The theater sells \(x\) adult tickets and \(y\) student tickets. Which expression represents the total revenue, and what additional equation is needed if exactly 80 tickets are sold?
discussion: Adult ticket revenue is \(14x\), and student ticket revenue is \(9y\).
The total revenue is \(14x+9y\).
Exactly 80 tickets means \(x+y=80\).

additionalPractice.question: A school's enrollment is modeled by \(E(t)=a+bt\), where \(t\) is the number of years after 2020. In 2020, enrollment was 840, and in 2024 it was 960. What is the predicted enrollment in 2030?
A farmer has chickens and goats. There are 38 animals and 104 legs in total. If \(c\) is the number of chickens and \(g\) is the number of goats, which system can be used to find \(c\) and \(g\)?
discussion: The total number of animals is \(c+g=38\).
Chickens contribute 2 legs each and goats contribute 4 legs each, so \(2c+4g=104\).

additionalPractice.question: A phone plan costs USD 35 for up to 4 gigabytes of data and USD 8 for every gigabyte above 4. Which expression gives the cost for \(x\) gigabytes when \(x>4\)?
discussion: The first 4 gigabytes are included in the USD 35 base cost.
The number of additional gigabytes is \(x-4\).
The cost is \(35+8(x-4)\).

additionalPractice.question: The number of students in a club is represented by \(n\). The statement “the number of students is at least 12 but less than 30” is written as:
discussion: “At least 12” includes 12, so \(n\ge12\).
“Less than 30” excludes 30, so \(n<30\).
Together, \(12\le n<30\).

additionalPractice.question: A quantity \(P\) is divided among \(x\) people. Each person receives 6 units, and 4 units remain. Which equation represents the situation?
discussion: The amount distributed to people is \(6x\).
There are 4 units left over, so the original quantity is \(P=6x+4\).

additionalPractice.question: A school can accept no more than 1,200 students. The number of boys is \(b\), the number of girls is \(g\), and the number of transfer students is \(t\). If the school must reserve at least 100 places for transfer students, which system describes the constraints?
discussion: The total enrollment cannot exceed 1,200, so \(b+g+t\le1200\).
At least 100 transfer places means \(t\ge100\).
Together, these constraints are option A.
